preparation.contract:
Tamir39Portfolio contact form — bounded interaction contract (draft)

Scope and evidence
This is a proposed interaction contract based on the task facts. It changes no project file, field schema, visual token, typography, spacing, color, icon set or motion language. Repository code, rendered UI and endpoint behavior were not inspected or tested. The portfolio is independent of Twohearts. No full design.md, backend feature or new library is required.

Authority and lifetime
The visitor owns the editable draft in page memory. A deliberate submission captures an immutable snapshot and a locally unique attempt token. That token correlates a response in this mounted form; it is not a server operation ID or duplicate-protection mechanism. The endpoint owns evidence of rejection or SMTP acceptance. The UI owns only waiting and presentation.

Keep the current attempt separate from the current draft. Editing while waiting changes only the draft. A completion for snapshot A never clears, replaces or marks later draft B as submitted. Preserve the draft even after acceptance; label the result as belonging to the submitted version. For example: “Submitted version accepted for sending. Your later edits have not been sent.” If unchanged: “Message accepted for sending. This does not confirm inbox delivery.”

Only current-attempt feedback and the current draft are retained in this form session. A deliberate new submission may replace earlier feedback and release the older snapshot. There is no operation history, reload-safe draft, cross-tab coordination or durable outcome recovery. Leaving/reloading may lose text and the current outcome; it neither cancels a dispatched message nor proves it was not sent. State these limits near the form, without adding a modal or a retention promise.

States and supported next actions
1. Ready: retain the existing fields, labels and validation rules. “Send message” validates the current draft, then captures and dispatches that snapshot once. Validation failure sends nothing and keeps all entered values. Explain each detected error beside its field with its existing accessible relationship; move focus to the first actionable invalid field after a deliberate failed submit.
2. Pending: action label “Sending…” and nearby status “Sending the submitted version. You can keep editing.” Keep fields editable. Keep the action discoverable with aria-disabled plus an actual activation guard. One guard covers pointer, keyboard, implicit submit and alternate entry points. Do not allow another send while locally pending. Routine status changes preserve focus. After 15 seconds, replace an active spinner with static “Still waiting for a response. This does not tell us whether your message was accepted.” This is a proposed feedback threshold, not a service timeout or permission to repeat. Continue waiting for the existing request's completion/transport timeout; no maximum wait or remote-stop guarantee is claimed.
3. Rejected — validation: show “This submitted version wasn’t accepted. Review the indicated fields.” Server errors belong to the submitted snapshot. If a field changed since dispatch, do not falsely mark its new value invalid; identify that the error concerned its submitted value, preserve the edit, and validate the current draft on the next deliberate attempt. The visitor can correct and submit again.
4. Rejected — rate limit: show “This attempt wasn’t accepted because too many messages were sent. Wait before sending again.” Follow an actual server-provided restriction or Retry-After when the endpoint supplies one. Do not invent a cooldown. Preserve the draft; allow a new deliberate submit only when known restrictions permit. A timer may re-enable a control but must never send.
5. Rejected — configuration: show “This attempt wasn’t accepted. The contact service is unavailable right now.” Preserve/edit/copy the draft and permit a deliberate attempt later. Do not claim the configuration is repaired, offer a fictional status check or automatically retry. A response qualifies for a rejection state only when its documented classification establishes that refusal before sending; a generic 5xx is not enough.
6. Accepted for sending: show “Message accepted for sending. This does not confirm inbox delivery.” Correlate it with the current submitted snapshot. Keep any newer draft unchanged. The visitor can edit, copy, leave, or deliberately submit another message. Sending unchanged content is another message; do not imply it updates, replaces or deduplicates the accepted one.
7. Unknown: a transport failure, ambiguous SMTP result, lost response or request timeout establishes no non-delivery claim. Show a persistent current-attempt warning: “We couldn’t confirm whether your message was accepted. Sending again could result in duplicate messages.” Preserve the draft. Do not label it “Failed to send,” “Not sent,” “Delivered,” or “Safe to retry.” There is no Check status control, operation reference, inbox-delivery guarantee or remote cancellation control.

Owner-approved deliberate repeat
The product owner explicitly accepts possible duplicate portfolio contact messages. This is the policy permitting a reduced capability for this contact action only. After Unknown, keep the warning visible while the visitor edits. Offer a warning-adjacent explicit action: “Send current message again” when unchanged, or “Send edited message” when changed. Explain beside it: “This sends the current fields as a new attempt. The earlier attempt may also have been accepted.”

A fresh intentional click, or Enter/Space while that explicit button is focused, is required after the warning is visible. Implicit Enter from an input must not silently dispatch the unknown repeat. Validate the then-current draft, capture a fresh snapshot, apply rate limits, and dispatch once. No automatic retry, replay on reconnect/reload, field-change submission or background resend is permitted. A warning acknowledges risk; it supplies no duplicate prevention and does not prove the first attempt failed.

There is one locally pending attempt at a time. A later result updates feedback only if it matches the currently tracked attempt. If it still matches an Unknown attempt and supplies authoritative acceptance, that current feedback may resolve to acceptance. Once the visitor deliberately starts a new attempt, an older completion cannot replace the new feedback or modify the draft. Current-attempt feedback can replace earlier feedback; previous uncertainty is not presented as resolved or preserved in an operation history. This bounded retention is an explicit consequence accepted by this task, including after a repeat.

Accessibility and visual behavior
Reuse current tokens and established controls; feedback is persistent text as well as any existing icon/color. Announce ordinary pending/result messages without moving focus, using the existing status region. Keep the repeat warning associated with its explicit action and keyboard reachable. Errors and service failures must not rely on color; service availability or uncertainty must not mark correct fields invalid. Preserve focus and selection where possible while the visitor edits. The existing validation owner must avoid competing native and custom announcements; verifying its exact implementation remains necessary. No new decorative animation, scale effect, icon treatment or dependency is introduced by this contract.

Contrast: charge with unknown outcome
For an overlapping charge with an unknown outcome, no duplicate protection and no owner-approved repeat policy, the next charge remains unavailable. Copy: “We can’t confirm whether the charge was made. Don’t submit it again here.” Keep the available in-session amount/target evidence and uncertainty visible; do not fabricate a transaction reference.

Supported actions are to read/copy available details, edit a prospective draft without dispatching it, or leave with the stated observation/recovery limits. A changed amount, another click, a fresh client token or a warning does not establish that the first charge did not occur. No automatic retry, generic Try again, new overlapping charge, cancellation claim, reversal claim, status lookup or support link is offered without actual capability and authorization.

No reconciliation route was supplied, so this contract promises none. The product/service owner must supply authoritative reconciliation or a verified service/approved risk policy before authorizing repeat dispatch. A memory-only frontend cannot enforce a financial gate across reloads, other tabs or devices; a repeat-capable charge flow must not be treated as ready to ship with that protection missing. Do not extend the portfolio's duplicate-message acceptance to payments. The safe immediate boundary is to leave repeat dispatch unavailable and explain why.

Verification and credits
This is document reasoning only. No rendered, keyboard, assistive-technology, backend or SMTP checks were performed. Before implementation is accepted, verify snapshot A plus edited B, implicit submit guards, authoritative pre-send rejection classifications, ambiguous SMTP/transport handling, actual rate-limit restrictions, focused deliberate repeat after its warning, stale completions, and the stated reload-loss behavior.

Methods used: scoped outcome evidence, draft/snapshot separation, limited retention, pending-action guards and owner-approved manual repetition from the local Atlas draft; restraint and preservation of project tokens from better-ui. Atlas knowledge is original synthesis by Tamir (Phi Vuong Tuong Tam), with Codex assistance, at the linked uncommitted draft snapshot. External authors are references, not endorsers. This output contains a new task-specific contract rather than copied source/library artifacts.

findings.title: Keep fixed overlays clear of the contact form at 320px
findings.requirementOrConcern: Project docs require pending feedback to remain visible; relevant responsive review must also check fixed controls against content rather than infer visibility from overflow assertions.
findings.trigger: At the supplied 320px contact-form scroll positions, the collapsed fixed Appearance trigger sits over the wrapped pending explanation. In the editorial dark accepted state, companion speech covers the form heading.
findings.consequence: Part of the explanation that edits are excluded from the pending send is covered. The companion can also obscure the form's identifying heading. Visitors have to scroll or dismiss an incidental overlay to see all the content.
evidence: Independently inspected supplement-pending-botanical-light-320.png: the circular Appearance trigger covers the left edge of wrapped pending copy.

appearance.css fixes a 44px opaque trigger near the lower-left viewport edge, including at mobile widths, without reserving contact-feedback clearance.

counterevidence: The supplied viewport-fit assertions pass, and the fields and submit control remain usable. Horizontal fit does not establish that foreground overlays leave copy unobscured.
The companion has an explicit dismiss button at CatCompanion.tsx:902, so its collision is recoverable.
The accepted status remains legible in the editorial screenshot. The stronger feedback-specific evidence is the botanical pending screenshot.
No baseline was inspected; this review does not establish that the collision was introduced by the contact-form changes.
findings.boundedCorrection: Give contact text and feedback a clear region while the form is in view: reposition or temporarily suppress overlapping fixed decorations/controls, and include the contact region in normal companion-bubble avoidance. Verify the collapsed Appearance control and companion reaction against pending and accepted states at 320px.
findings.standardClassification: Supported usability concern and project visibility contract; not a universal visual-style rule or asserted WCAG failure.

supportedContractChecks.evidence: FormData captures the outgoing fields before awaiting. A monotonic edit revision preserves all current fields after any edit, including edit then revert. Supplied assertions report snapshot A, edited B and reverted-draft preservation passing.
Unedited success resets the form. The first subsequent edit marks the draft unsent; subsequent typing does not repeatedly change status. Supplied assertions pass.

A synchronous ref gates every form submission; the pending button's click handler also prevents activation. Supplied rapid-click and Enter assertion reports one request while pending; button remains focusable with aria-disabled.

400/429/503 explicitly report unsent attempts. Other HTTP failures and connection loss preserve the draft and warn that another manual send could duplicate delivery. No automatic retry or delivery lookup is promised. The route returns 200 after sendMail resolves and 502 on caught send failure. Real service acceptance was not exercised.

Labelled native fields, mounted polite status and alert, busy state confined to the button, static pending text and reduced-motion/user-motion-off spinner handling are present. Supplied assertions cover persistent regions, retained keyboard focus, continued editing, no repeated status mutation, forced colors and motion-off.
